newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials down, TZI well received.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials down, TZI well received.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrial shares finished Thursday weaker amid small volumes with Trans Zambezi Industries (TZI) staging a brilliant listing debut, dealers said.

"Trade was a little quiet across the market in small volumes. Industrials were a little weak but volumes were very small," one dealer said. "Friday might see trade pick up a little bit and indices could move up," he added.
Dealers said that TZI, which made its debut on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Thursday, was the feature of the day and saw 3.6 million shares change hands.
"It was a very successful listing," one dealer said.
TZI was listed at 4,000 cents and closed trade at 5,200.
The industrial index lost 75.99 points to close at 10,648.35 points.
Meikles and UDC finished at previous closing levels in reasonable turnover. Dunlop added 10 cents to 210 cents.
But Barclays shed 50 cents to 3,650 cents, CAPS lost 35 cents to 1,325 cents and FMB cut 200 cents to 5,800 cents.
The small mining index inched up 12.11 points to 895.00 with Ashanti and Wankie both trading unchanged, while Falgold put on five cents to 70 cents and Rio Tinto rose 100 cents to 2,000 cents.
